To study the feasibility of memristor-based optical synapses in SNNs, a behavior model for optoelectronic memristors is proposed in this paper, including electrical programming modeling and photocurrent read modeling. Based on the model, the behavior of a molecular ferroelectric (MF)/semiconductor interfacial memristor is simulated. This paper also proposes an optical synaptic circuit for trace-based spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) learning rule. The electrical characteristics of the memristor are explored and exploited to emulate the trace in the pairwise nearest-neighbor STDP, while the optical characteristics are utilized for non-destructive readout and weight calculation. Synaptic-level simulation results show a 99.96% correlation coefficient (CC) and a 1.91% relative root mean square error (RRMSE) in the weight approximate computation. Extending the simulation to the network level, the optoelectronic memristor-based unsupervised STDP learning system can achieve a 92.07± 0.64% accuracy on the MNIST benchmark.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a 7 Gb/s Rotatable Non-contact Connector with Grid Array Package Application
abstract: A 7 Gb/s compact rotatable transmission line coupler (RTLC) is developed for grid array applications and is suitable for high-speed multi-pin FPGA packages. The miniaturized RTLC operates in a new deep proximity coupling mode, achieving high coupling gain and wide bandwidth simultaneously. Ground shielding vias provide return paths for signal vias, which achieves better impedance matching and suppresses signal reflection to 1/18. Following miniaturization, a prototype of a 4x4 grid array with a pitch of 1 mm is fabricated. In terms of crosstalk performance, the RTLC-grid array exhibits robustness against horizontal offsets of up to 10% of the pitch and vertical offsets of up to 33% of the communication distance, even under the most severe conditions.

articleTitle: A New Current-Mode Subthreshold, High-PSRR MOSFET-Only Bandgap Voltage Reference
abstract: A new CMOS MOSFET-only bandgap voltage reference that operates at low voltage, provides low power, and is insensitive to temperature changes, is presented in this paper. To save chip area and simplify the design, the circuit is implemented with subthreshold MOSFETs instead of bulky Bipolar junction transistors (BJT). The circuit, designed using 130 nm CMOS technology, generates a voltage reference of 593 mV and a temperature coefficient of 7S ppm in the range of-2 $0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $90^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, without trimmings. Post-layout simulation results show that the circuit achieves a high power supply rejection ratio (PSRR) of -87dB at low frequencies. The proposed circuit draws a current of 3.7 $\mu$A from a 1.2 V power supply.

articleTitle: Training Low-Latency Spiking Neural Network with Orthogonal Spiking Neurons
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) as a biology-inspired method mimicking the signal transmission of brain neurons can be managed in an event-driven manner, and generate binary signals that are computing-friendly to hardware by their recurrent time window. However, training high-performing SNNs from scratch emerges intrinsic defects, a large number of time steps (>100) is unable to balance the performance with latency. To overcome this issue, we show that SNNs can be trained in fewer time steps (<4) through the proposed Alterable Space-Time LIF (AST-LIF) block, which transforms partial time steps into the space domain. AST-LIF iterates the signals in horizontal and vertical directions in a time step unit, and utilizes the global dependency as Long short-term memory (LSTM) model in a space step unit. Our approach aims to significantly reduce SNNs latency while ensuring high performance. For proof-of-concept, extensive experiments show that balanced spatio-temporal architecture can maintain the performance of SNNs with smaller time steps $(t=2)$.

articleTitle: A Fast Approach to Droplet Routing with Shape-Dependent Velocity on MEDA Biochips
abstract: Due to the development of biochips, which play a significant role in Point of Care Testing such as PCR testing, they can provide faster and experiments with fewer reagents compared with conventional experiments. To enhance the advantage of such biochips, there have appeared myriad works that further extract the potential on biochips. This paper presents a fast algorithm for droplet routing problems on MEDA biochips, where routing considers droplet velocity dependent on its shape. Our proposed algorithm has achieved more than 99% reduction of computational runtime compared with the state-of-the-art method based on integer linear programming.

articleTitle: A Computationally Efficient Predistortion and Segment Thresholding for Distributed PA Arrays
abstract: Multipath MIMO systems have emerged, providing faster and more reliable wireless communications. These systems require distributed arrays of nonlinear power amplifiers, which in turn require novel digital predistortion solutions. In this paper the authors propose a novel technique called, variation in the slope, to reduce the computational overhead of multipath segmented DPD for distributed arrays of power amplifiers. Additionally the approach to calculate the threshold for the segments requires only the second derivative calculation of gain versus input power and thus avoids computationally expensive clustering techniques. This approach was validated using a 100MHz5G NR signal and a hybrid beam former module, resulting in an achieved −50dB ACLR on average. This value meets the spectral mask requirement for 5GFR2 standards. This method requires fewer training samples and DPD parameters compared to state-of-the-art techniques for multipath systems.

articleTitle: A Low-Voltage Submicrowatt, High-Speed CMOS Dynamic Comparator
abstract: We present an energy-efficient dynamic comparator that is suitable for low-voltage and high-speed applications. The preamplifier circuit prevents fully discharging the output nodes without utilizing an extra capacitor, which improves power consumption and operating speed compared to other solutions. The comparator is designed in a 65-nm CMOS technology at a power supply of1.2 V. The designed comparator operates at a frequency of 1.2 MHz, consumes 931.1 nW, and has a delay of 0.64 ns at $\Delta \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{i}\mathrm{n}}$=1mV. To estimate the offset of the proposed circuit, Monte Carlo simulations were performed and resulted in a standard deviation of 1.54 mV and a mean of 1.06 mV.

articleTitle: A 40 nA, 84% Efficient, PLL-based Rectifier-Less Power Switching Converter for Low-Voltage Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting
abstract: We proposed a PLL-based rectifier-less interface circuit to control the power switches for harvesting energy from a low-voltage piezoelectric transducer with input power levels of 100 nW to 40 $\mu$W. In this proposed method, charge-pump PLL is first locked with the input frequency of the PEH to detect its peak output voltage for maximum power extraction. Once locked, power transfer occurs where PLL is operated in an open-loop (only VCO is functional) to minimize the power loss. In 180 nm CMOS technology, the power switching converter was designed and extracts power with a minimum piezoelectric open-circuit voltage of 0.17 V. At an input power of 10 $\mu$W and a vibration frequency of 88 Hz, it achieves a maximum power efficiency of 84%. The control unit consumes an average current of 40 nA from a 1.5 V output voltage over a broad input power range.

articleTitle: Adaptive FOCV MPPT for Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting Circuit
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive fractional open circuit voltage MPPT algorithm for maximizing power output of piezoelectric energy harvesting systems by adjusting the output voltage of the rectifier circuit. The algorithm measures the charge loss duration, enabling effective tracking only when excitation changes. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art MPPT algorithms in terms of power efficiency, circuit simplicity, and sampling time, and confirms its effectiveness in enhancing the performance of piezoelectric energy harvesting systems.

articleTitle: A 3.3V Saturation-Aware Neurostimulator with Reset Functionality in 22 nm FDSOI
abstract: Neurostimulation and extensive signal processing are requirements for closed-loop neural interfaces. At the same time, issues of thermal biocompatibility limit the power budget in such applications, driving the trend towards small technologies like 22 nm FDSOI. While overcoming aforementioned constraints, this trend complicates the design of current stimulators with up to 3. 3V supply voltage in such technology. Stacking of 1.8 V compliant IO-transistors, is part of the solution. In this work we address this challenge, showcasing a small footprint neurostimulator design (0.0128 $mm^{2}$) in 22 nm FDSOI, capable of detecting source saturation, a safe reset state and the generation of arbitrary multi-channel stimulation waveforms. The DNL and INL of the output current are in the range of ±0.45 LSB and ±2.2 LSB respectively. The output current range of ±186$\mu \mathrm{A}$ is divided into 63 steps.

articleTitle: Efficiency and Sustainability in Simulation: Enhancing Accuracy of Chaotic Maps Using Kahan Summation
abstract: Mathematical modelling is essential in scientific research for approximating systems through equations for simulation, prediction, and investigation. While system identification techniques have become popular for obtaining models directly from data, finding an appropriate model for nonlinear systems can be difficult. In particular, conventional model validation approaches are ineffective for chaotic systems. Although numerical simulations are widely used to identify and analyse these mathematical models, less attention has been given to improving simulation accuracy, leading to imprecise results. This work proposes an efficient and sustainable approach to improve the accuracy of chaotic maps by reducing numerical errors and increasing precision during simulations of chaotic polynomial models. The Kahan summation is used to minimise the propagation of computational error, and the results are validated using symbolic computation. The proposed technique increases simulation accuracy, allows more iterates with no loss of digit significance, and represents a way to save energy by requiring less powerful computing. The main contribution of this work is the presentation of an effective method for reducing the influence of numerical errors, a simple mathematical tool with low computational cost. Future investigations could focus on the reduction in LLE despite the Kahan summation not changing the mathematical map.

articleTitle: American Sign Language Recognition System Using Wearable Sensors and Machine Learning
abstract: This paper describes a recognition system that is designed to aid users of American Sign Language. American Sign Language is growing in popularity, and such systems can be used to help improve the communication barrier between ASL sign language users and people who don't understand the language. The proposed preliminary system is designed to detect ten words in the ASL language. Sensors positioned on both wrists are used to collect data that will reflect the motions of the hands. The data is processed and trained using the Support Vector Machine, and Discriminant analysis classifiers using a selective combination of features were explored. Data was collected with Inertial Measurement Unit sensors strapped on the index and middle fingers to simulate a wearable ring. This data, combined with the data collected from the wrists, are trained using the Discriminant analysis classifier, and the system achieved a classification accuracy of 82%.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Graphite Based Flexible Thermoplastic Polyurethane Electromyography Electrode
abstract: 3D printed electrodes could enable many opportunities in the field of personalized myoelectrical prosthesis. The design and the assay of 3D printed electrodes with and without gold-plated skin interface are described in this study. The signal strength and quality of 3D printed electrodes have been assessed by comparing them to a standard Ag/AgCl electromyography electrode type. Results confirm the great potential of using this method as an alternative to electrode production.

articleTitle: A 10Bit 6 GS/s Time-Interleaved SAR ADC with a Single Full-Rate Front-End Track-and-Hold
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband 10bit 6GS/s time-interleaved successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) implemented in a standard 28nm CMOS technology. The single front-end top-plate track-and-hold circuit (T/H) provides 17.4GHz sampling bandwidth, $\gt 70$ dB linearity in spite of the 75ps tracking duration and adequate kickback isolation while driving twelve 500MS/s SAR-ADC lanes. Utilizing a full-rate front-end sampler at 6GS/s simplifies the overall ADC calibration scheme as both, timing- and bandwidth mismatch are eliminated. Each SAR-ADC lane takes advantage of a capacitive sub-2 radix digital-to-analog converter (C-DAC) topology with 6.5% over-range to handle C-DAC mismatch effects as well as finite settling while a fully loop-unrolled comparator architecture with multiple latches maximizes the sampling rate and linearity. The SAR-ADC system operates from a 2.5V/1.8V/1V/-1.3V power supply consuming in total 1.2W. The ADC achieves an excellent spectral performance with a SNDR and SFDR of 54.8dB and 69.5dBc respectively, using a single full scale $1\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{ppd}}$ sine wave tone close to Nyquist frequency after C-DAC mismatch, time-interleaved gain and offset mismatch calibration.

articleTitle: Frequency and noise characterization for baseband signal processing on neuromorphic circuits
abstract: Memristor crossbar-based systems have shown enor-mous potential to further enhance applications that make extensive use of vector-matrix multiplication, such as artificial in neural networks. Many signal processing algorithms in wireless communications, such as forward error correction (FEC) and discrete Fourier transform (DFT), involve such operations and could benefit from the desirable properties of memristor crossbars, namely, low power consumption, low latency and high area density. We investigate the high data rate response of memristor crossbars including line parasitic resistance and capacitance, for FEC and DFT applications in baseband signal processing for wireless communications.

articleTitle: Efficient Transistor-Level QDI Asynchronous Switch for Neuromorphic Systems
abstract: Neuromorphic systems benefit from quasi-delay-insensitive (QDI) asynchronous interconnection networks, which offer low power consumption, improved robustness, and scalability. However, when designing Networks-on-Chip (NoC) routers with standard multiplexer cell-based switches, asynchronous circuits suffer from area overhead and power consumption. To address this issue, we propose a transistor-level asynchronous switch design that reduces the number of control signals, resulting decrease in transistor count by 36%. By decomposing those control signals, we achieved a power consumption reduction of 77% and improved delay by 18%. The transistor-level switch was designed using the Sense Amplifier Half-Buffer (SAHB) logic family, and its performance was simulated using models for 65-nanometer CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Improved Dynamic Comparator With Adaptive Delay Line for the Latch Conduction and Regenerative Feedback Assisted FIA
abstract: This article presents a low-noise energy-efficient comparator design. Firstly, by using an adaptive delay line based on the differential voltage at the output of the pre-amplifier, the delayed clock turns on the latch stage after the pre-amplifier stage where the delay is automatically changed depending on the input voltage level. Secondly, a regenerative feedback assisted Dynamic Floating Inverter Amplifier (FIA) is used to increase integration speed and gain. For Successive-approximation-register (SAR) ADCs where each bit is determined sequentially and the input voltage level differs in each cycle, the comparator resolves small analog inputs up to twice per conversion theoretically. The time taken by the proposed comparator to resolve analog input into digital output (called CLK-OUT delay) only increases in the small signal voltage range (near its input-referred noise level) which has less impact on SAR ADCs sample rate. The proposed comparator in 28 nm process technology achieves 66.37-uV input-referred noise while consuming approximately 780 fJ per comparison under a 0.9-V supply. This represents greater than 20-time energy efficiency boost compared to the previous comparator with a dynamic floating inverter pre-amplifier.

articleTitle: A 4 GBaud 5 Vpp Class-B Pre-Driver Design for GaN-Based Switching Power Amplifier in 22 nm SOI-CMOS Utilizing LDMOS
abstract: The paper presents a highly power efficient class-B LDMOS-based pre-driver, implemented in a 22nm FDSOI CMOS process. The driver generates an output voltage swing of 5. 5V at a data-rate of 4 GBaud for GaN-based switching power amplifier with an estimated capacitive load impedance of 0.35 pF. This is achieved by utilizing monolithical integrated LDMOS devices with a breakdown voltage of 6.5 V, available in the deep submicron state-of-the-art CMOS process, which are driven by an inverter-chain consisting of 2V thick-oxide devices with an active back-gate control to implement a duty-cycle calibration. The proposed design achieves rise- and fall-times of 70ps and 40 ps, respectively. The total power consumption is below 140 mW from a triple 5. 5V, 3.5V and 2V power supply for a 4 GBaud NRZ PRBS input. This greatly improves the state-of-the-art power efficiency for CMOS-based GaN power amplifier predriver.

Index Terms: Laterally Diffused Metal Oxide Semiconductor Device

articleTitle: UPF-Aware CDC Structural Verification on RTL
abstract: Current ICs (Integrated Circuits) include millions-of-gates IPs (Intellectual Properties) that interface to each other through multiple asynchronous clock domains. Therefore, to ensure the correctness of the asynchronous communications, exhaustive CDC (Clock Domain Crossing) structural verification must be performed. The target of this verification is to detect all possible CDC paths present in a design. This requires all clocks to be well defined and concurrently propagated. Including the UPF (Unified Power Format) file is crucial for such a verification. The presence of these low-power components poses a new challenge for the CDC structural verification. However, their absence risks masking a considerable number of CDC problems. An open Tcl tool allowing the elaboration of additional and custom features is used to demonstrate how our approach increased the QoR (Quality of Results) compared to the native platform.

articleTitle: A flexible Power Management System-On-Chip for Implantable Brain-Machine-Interfaces
abstract: Implantable electronics are found manifold in literature. While most published work focuses on the sensing and driving interfaces e.g., in neural recording or neuromodulation systems, the surrounding system functions are often neglected or treated as incidental. In many devices, the power management circuits are realized with off-the-shelf components as this is quick and flexible, but it comes at the cost of area, volume and power inefficiency. While many tailored solutions for implantable power management integrated circuits (ICs) have been proposed in literature, a circuit combining many of the needed functions in a flexible way, such that it is reusable for various applications, is the goal of this work. We thus propose a power management IC for a neural implant, which is designed to accommodate most of the required functionality, while requiring only few external components. The system is highly flexible and can be programmed via SPI. A prototype in 180nm HV-CMOS occupies 2.56 mm$^{2}$ and provides 7 LDOs (5 programmable), a HV shunt regulator, current monitoring, and a temperature sensor.

articleTitle: Pose Aware RGBD-based Face Recognition System With Hierarchical Bilinear Pooling
abstract: The accuracy of face recognition is not satisfactory in large poses. It is because the existing face recognition methods rely only on RGB images, which lose information in the large head pose. Therefore, we utilize depth images containing 3D dimension information to complement the loss. In this work, we propose a pose-invariant RGBD face recognition method with the Hierarchical Bilinear Pooling module (HBP) and Pose-Aware Module (PAM). Most of the existing methods consider the final layer of the model. However, the final layer does not contain enough facial information, such as the eyes, nose, and mouth. Thus, we propose the HBP module to fuse high-level layers which can focus on important facial areas but with different perspectives than the final layer. To reduce the effect of head poses, we propose the PAM module via mapping the profile faces to frontal faces in feature space. We verify our method on the datasets proposed by [1] and KinectFaceDB [2]. Our method achieves 1.3% improvement and has 6.1 million fewer parameters than the method in [3].

articleTitle: Nano-Magnetic Logic based Architecture for Edge Inference using Tsetlin Machine
abstract: High learning accuracy with less time, low energy and small memory footprint made Tsetlin Machine (TM) an emerging edge inference alternative to traditional machine learning algorithms such as neural networks (NN). Advances in nanomagnetic logic are considered a potential alternative to CMOS-based digital circuits due to their non-volatility, low power and high integration density. Adapting the advantages of these two technologies, we propose a novel nano-magnetic logic-based architecture for edge inference using the Tsetlin machine to build energy-efficient applications. This design can be expanded to construct energy-efficient Convolution TM applications. The proposed TM inference architecture is designed by exploiting the shape and positional hybrid anisotropy and the antifer-romagnetically coupled fixed input majority gate (MG). The micromagnetic tool is used for the simulation framework. The proposed design to implement 2 clause TM inference requires 15 majority gates comprising a total of 60 nanomagnets and 14 interconnect magnets, requiring $1.24X10^{-19}J$ energy per operation which is $10^{5}$ to $10^{6}$ times less compared to CMOS logic, and the power consumed by the total number of nanomagnets for implementing the proposed architecture is 0.00082 $\mu \mathrm{W}$.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Secure Circuit Styles Using Unipolar Logic Gates
abstract: A high level of resistance against power analysis attacks can be achieved with secure circuit styles. All existing secure circuit styles are based on CMOS logic, using both p-type and n-type transistors. However, emerging technologies, such as flexible electronics, achieve optimal price, performance and reliability with n-type-only unipolar logic gates. Therefore, in order to protect chips on flexible foil from power analysis attacks, secure circuit styles based on unipolar logic gates need to be considered. This paper presents a first step in this direction by applying the concepts of secure circuit styles, originally designed with CMOS logic in mind, to unipolar gates. The power consumption information leakage is simulated for two existing secure circuit styles, namely Wave Dynamic Differential Logic (WDDL) and Masked Dual-Rail Pre-charge Logic (MDPL). The paper shows that especially WDDL has the potential to improve the security of the design, after optimization of the transistor ratios.

articleTitle: A Low-Noise CMOS Front-End with 534 MΩ Transimpedance Gain for Single-Molecule Signal Acquisition
abstract: We designed and characterized a low-noise RTIA (transimpedance amplifier) with $534 \mathrm{M}\Omega$ transimpedance gain fabricated in a $0.18- \mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS process for pA signal acquisition, which lay the foundation for nanopore sequencing. A feedback resistance with $268 \mathrm{M}\Omega$ and source degeneration were firstly demonstrated to suppress the input referred noise. Next, dual-end output configuration was adapted for doubling the actual signal gain. Finally, we show an output buffer with the gain of 17 dB leading to $7 \times$ equivalent feedback capacitance can be utilized for boosting the bandwidth. Our experimental results confirm that this amplifier design can detect the interaction between DNA molecules and the nanopore sensor. The noise level of our system exhibits 5.5 pA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RMS</inf> (<1 kHz) and 14.1 pA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RMS</inf> (<5 kHz), which is in a reasonable agreement with our control tests on the “gold standard” Axo-patch 200B amplifier.

articleTitle: Triple Clock Boosted Voltage Multiplier: A Design Strategy to Heavily Reduce Rise Time
abstract: This paper introduces a Dickson voltage multiplier topology which includes a triple voltage booster to achieve better performance in terms of speed at the same maximum output voltage and silicon-occupied area. The proposed solution comes with an optimization design strategy that maximizes the advantages given by the applied clock boosting technique. The comparison with the conventional design demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed solution. Such comparison is carried out by simulating the two topologies by using the 65-nm CMOS technology provided by STMicroelectronics.

articleTitle: Overview of Memristive Cryptography
abstract: Memristors are emerging nano-devices with potential for excellent performance and rich electrical dynamic behavior. After their numerous successful applications in neu-romorphic and in-memory computing, the scientific community has turned to their potential for cryptographic implementations. This overview aims at summarizing the current state of affairs in this domain and outlining possible directions for future research. As in other fields where researchers from different disciplines come together, tensions and misunderstandings with respect to objectives and terminology are unavoidable, including the precise meaning of the very term “memristive cryptography”. We aim at establishing a better understanding of the objectives followed by various strands of research. An important issue is to synchronize recently reported results with the established requirements and performance indicators from the classical cryptography domain. As a specific example, we consider random number generation for security applications, which is one main line of memristive cryptography research. We outline today's requirements on RNGs that are enforced by RNG standards and therefore are a prerequisite for the practical relevance of any such developments in the medium-to-long term.
